sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface HA signal detected on non-permeabilized cells by immunofluorescence (L3); quantified HA/V5 fluorescence intensity ratio across 10 cells confirms HA is extracellular and V5 is intracellular (L7). Membrane trafficking confirmed by co-localisation of JAM2-V5 with PH-GFP membrane marker (L4). Wild-type and disease-variant (R108H, W168C) constructs bearing the same dual-tag were compared for membrane localisation (L5); no untagged control comparison reported.
sites.rationale: JAM2 is a type-I single-pass transmembrane protein; its signal peptide spans residues 1–28 (authoritative landmarks), placing the mature N-terminus at residue 29 (F). An HA tag at the amino terminus of the full-length construct must therefore sit after residue 28 to survive signal-peptide cleavage and reach the extracellular face. Python confirms seq[28]='G' and seq[29]='F'. The paper's L2 text erroneously labels this terminus 'intracellular', but the direct experimental evidence in L3 (anti-HA staining of non-permeabilized cells) and L7 (quantified HA/V5 ratio) unambiguously demonstrates extracellular surface display of the HA tag. The insertion site is 211 residues from the TM boundary, satisfying the ≥3-residue constraint. Full-length JAM2 was expressed in mammalian cells with an HA tag at the amino terminus (after the signal peptide, residues 1–28) and a V5 tag at the carboxyl terminus. Non-permeabilized cells were stained with anti-HA before permeabilization, directly demonstrating cell-surface accessibility of the N-terminal HA tag. The paper names no specific residue number for the insertion; JAM2 has exactly one extracellular terminus (the mature N-terminus after signal cleavage at residue 28), so the junction is topology-derived as insert_after_residue=28.

sources.claim: For surface HA detection, non‐permeabilized cells were stained with anti‐HA (1:1000, Cell Signaling Technology) before permeabilization and V5 labeling.

literature_notes: All seven ledger lines derive from a single paper (PMC13521667). L1 describes a commercial Origene pCMV V5-JAM2 construct with no stated tag position and therefore cannot alone pin a residue. L2–L7 together define a dual-tagged full-length JAM2: HA at the amino terminus (extracellular, confirmed by surface staining) and V5 at the carboxyl terminus (intracellular, confirmed by the HA/V5 topology assay). L2 contains an apparent textual inversion ('V5 at extracellular C-terminus, HA at intracellular N-terminus') that contradicts the experimental results in L3 and L7; the functional data are taken as authoritative. The C-terminal V5 tag is intracellular and is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion for JAM2, so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal V5 tag is intracellular, confirmed by the HA/V5 topology assay showing V5 is accessible only after permeabilization; the intracellular domain spans residues 259–298.
